_comment: REAL SHAPE, INVENTED VALUES. The key names and value types of api2.cursor.sh's aiserver.v1.DashboardService/GetCurrentPeriodUsage, captured with `npm run probe -- --keys` on the owner's own Mac (2026-09-20, Cursor Free plan). The probe prints key names and types and never a value, so every number, boolean and string below is invented: what is real is that these keys exist, with these types, and that the public trackers' `planUsage.limit`, `totalSpend` and top-level percentages do not. The values are chosen to exercise all three rows parseCursorUsage can build — a plan percentage, an Auto percentage that differs from it (the Free-plan case), and an on-demand cap with `overallLimit` above zero.
_comment_strings: Every string value is tagged STRINGVALUE- and padded to a plausible length for the field, the convention claude-web-usage-live-keys.json set: a leak into a log line is then unmissable, and nothing may ever branch on one. `billingCycleStart` and `billingCycleEnd` are the two exceptions and are real RFC 3339 dates, because `billingCycleEnd` is parsed — it becomes the `resetsAt` of the two window rows, and a tagged string there would only pin the malformed-date path the suite tests separately.
